title: Semantic Granularity Navigation in Image Editing
claim: Coupling edit progress to scale causes drift and leakage into unedited regions, while decoupling preserves structure and still applies the edit.
layout: 2 rows by 3 columns, left-to-right, red boxes mark artifacts
description: The figure is a 2×3 grid of photographs. The columns are labeled "Real Image", "Coupled Edit" and "Decoupled Edit". The top row is a plate of rolled wraps, with the edit "rolled wraps -> steak" written in handwritten text beneath it. The bottom row is a white horse in an orange sunset field, with the edit "horse -> zebra" beneath it. In the Coupled Edit column, thick red boxes highlight the failures. On the plate, the table and plate geometry have shifted. On the horse, a ghosted second head and a duplicated zebra face appear, so the edit has leaked into other areas. The Decoupled Edit column shows a clean steak and a single zebra with the original background and layout intact. The eye goes first to the red boxes in the middle column, then compares across to the clean right column.
caption: Coupling vs. decoupling. Under the same model and step budget, coupled scale–progress editing exhibits drift/leakage into non-edited regions (red boxes), while decoupled navigation preserves structure while executing the semantic change.
abstract: Despite the generative capabilities of diffusion and flow models, real-image editing remains constrained by a persistent trade-off between semantic editability and structural fidelity. We trace a primary cause of this limitation to the implicit coupling of edit progress with model scale in existing paradigms. Under this coupling, stronger edits typically require visiting noisier states, which spends computation on destabilizing layout before the semantic change is well localized. We introduce NaviEdit, a training-free inference-time controller that decouples edit progress from model scale traversal through a strict self-consistency contract. NaviEdit operates at the rollout level and leaves the underlying pretrained model unchanged. It treats scale as a control input and reallocates a fixed step budget toward semantically responsive intermediate scales instead of destructive high-noise regimes. Experiments show positive average gains across compatible editors and flow backbones, supporting decoupling as a portable inference-time control principle.
